questions.q: The Store Operations lead asks, "Can you tell me how we did yesterday?" What should happen next?
options: Tell the Store Operations lead the question is too vague to answer
Build the pipeline first, then ask questions only if the numbers look wrong
Start writing PySpark immediately so there's something to show
Ask follow-up questions to turn the vague request into a specific, answerable requirement
questions.explain: A short clarifying conversation up front prevents guessing wrong on source, grain, metric definition, or cadence and finding out only after the pipeline is already running.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four things this lesson says to pin down before writing any code?
options: Which cloud region the Spark cluster runs in
Which systems count as sources (in-store POS, online storefront, or both)
What grain the result is built at (one row per what)
How often the pipeline needs to refresh
questions.explain: The four things to clarify are source, grain, metric definition, and refresh cadence — cluster region isn't a requirements-clarification question for this project.

questions.q: Why does this lesson choose "one row per calendar day" as the grain, rather than one row per store or per line item?
options: Because PySpark cannot group by more than one column at a time
Because this is the smallest, first version of the pipeline, meant to answer one honest daily number before narrowing to finer detail later
Because the Store Operations lead explicitly forbade any per-store breakdown
Because Delta Lake cannot store more than one row per day in a table
questions.explain: The lesson deliberately keeps the grain coarse for this first pipeline — later projects in the track narrow it to per-line-item detail.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly named as a known limitation this project leaves out, rather than silently ignores?
options: Returns and refunds adjustments to the sales total
Combining in-store and online sales into one number
Writing the result as a Delta table
Running the pipeline once a day
questions.explain: The lesson flags returns/refunds handling as a deliberate out-of-scope limitation, named out loud rather than hidden.

questions.q: What does "refresh cadence" mean in the final written requirement?
options: The maximum file size allowed in the Bronze layer
How often the pipeline re-runs and what time window each run covers
The font and color scheme used on the final Power BI report
The number of Delta tables the pipeline writes
questions.explain: Refresh cadence is specifically about run frequency and the time window each run is responsible for — here, once a day, covering the previous full day.
